Two photon electromagnetically induced transparency with counter propagating beams is the standard readout. EIT linewidth sets energy resolution. Single atom selection can narrow linewidth to the Rydberg decay rate order, yet thermal Doppler shifts broaden it to the intermediate state decay rate order. The authors derive an analytic form for the Doppler leftover profile at low power. For rubidium, the FWHM limit is 1.84 MHz, slightly above which the measured linewidth sits, about twice narrower than before.
arxiv-2603-05496: Khesin and Lu introduce mirror codes, a flexible LDPC stabilizer code family built from a group and two subsets whose total size bounds the check weight. The family covers every abelian two-block group algebra code, yet its members are manifestly not CSS in general. Fixing check weight 6 yields several non-CSS codes, and syndrome extraction circuits trade overhead for provable fault tolerance. End-to-end quantum memory experiments reach an error pseudothreshold around 0.2%, approximately matching the [[144, 12, 12]] bivariate bicycle code under the same noise model.
arxiv-2603-05596: Hopp and colleagues present X-SORTER, a program identifying galaxy cluster mergers from optical binarity indicators in the redMaPPer catalog. Merging clusters probe dark matter interactions through offsets among galaxies, the intracluster medium, and the dark matter halo. They select clusters where the leading brightest cluster galaxy probability falls below 0.98 and optical richness exceeds 120. Observations with XMM and Keck/DEIMOS cover twelve clusters lacking previous XMM-Newton or Chandra archival data and show most targets morphologically disturbed. Several post-pericenter, dissociative systems show X-ray peaks between galaxies.
arxiv-2603-05696: Yin and team present Ptychi-Evolve, using language models to find and evolve smoothing rules for imaging. Ptychography is computer imaging for sharp materials, where rebuilds often require hand-set smoothing functions. Its design pairs LLM-driven code making with breeding crossover and changes. Tests on X-ray joined circuits, low-dose apoferritin views, and multi-layer imaging with crosstalk flaws show found smoothers beating standard rebuilds. Gains reach up to +0.26 SSIM, with higher PSNR. Ptychi-Evolve also logs code family trees and growth data for clear, re-doable analysis.
arxiv-2603-05796: Peng and team use guided flow matching to turn cone-beam CT scans into fake CT images for ray therapy. Cone-beam scans support patient lining up but suffer severe flaws and wrong Hounsfield units, limiting number use. Their model slowly transforms a normal-spread sample into a CT image tuned to the input scan. Tests on brain, head-and-neck, and lung patients show flaw cut, with error, signal-to-noise, and link metrics rising. The fake images support better organ splitting and dose math for live ray therapy.
arxiv-2603-05896: Hyland and team report new VLBA shift and motion measurements of BeSSeL Survey masers: three water masers and one methanol maser. These shifts, combined with 3D motion distances, sharpen the Perseus arm's place and pitch angle in the first galaxy quadrant. Pushing the Perseus and Sagittarius arm spots beyond the Center, they find the arms crossing at an about Galactocentric angle of 200 degrees and radius of 5.6 kpc.
arxiv-2603-05996: Chen and team propose Track-SQL, boosting making models with dual-pulling modules tracking schema and context in multi-turn Text-to-SQL. Making models show promise in single-turn Text-to-SQL, but not as much in multi-turn settings, from weakness handling context and dynamic schema linking. Track-SQL adds a Meaning-boosted Schema Puller and a Schema-aware Context Puller. Tests show state-of-the-art scores on SparC and CoSQL. Cut-out studies reveal improved multi-turn running score by 7.1 percent and above 9 percent in turn.
arxiv-2603-06496: Kerkelä and Zhang address microstructure estimation under acquisition protocols, where learning methods fail from scan rules and need retraining when scans change. They present a graph neural network showing data as a point cloud in three-dimensional measurement space, with rotation-proof message passing and permutation-proof pooling into tissue codes. Guided by physics and symmetries rather than generic designs, the model trains on simulated data. It works on unseen real-world scans without new training, toward train-once-deploy-anywhere mapping for use.
arxiv-2604-00196: Montefusco and two colleagues revise a nuclear metamodel that is not relativistic, tightening its high-density behavior and its match to equations of state built from microscopic physics. Because causality at high density is built in, far fewer models get tossed for faster-than-light sound speeds. That eases study of equilibrium neutron star setups. The framework also supports Bayesian inference of neutron star traits beyond masses and radii, probing quantities that depend on composition. These include the dUrca threshold, plus the Ledoux criterion for g-mode stability.
arxiv-2604-00696: Jahagirdar and colleagues present TTA-Vid, test-time adaptation for video reasoning. Video reasoning models perform on temporal and multimodal understanding, yet need supervised datasets and staged training, making them costly and hard to adapt to new domains. TTA-Vid adapts a pretrained model to video samples as they arrive, with no labels, using reinforcement learning at test time on video-language data. It pairs step-by-step reasoning at inference over frame subsets with a batch-aware frequency-based reward across subsets as ground truth for updates.
arxiv-2604-00796: Ali and colleagues tackle budget splitting across billboards and social media, asking how a commercial house should divide spending to maximize total influence. They define an interaction effect for extra influence from combined media triggers. Their influence function is non-negative, monotone, and non-bisubmodular. Randomized Greedy and Two-Phase Adaptive Greedy methods then deliver a provable approximation guarantee, and real-data tests beat existing approaches.
arxiv-2604-00896: Jia and colleagues design a double breast gradient coil for diffusion-weighted imaging that controls front-to-back gradient variation. An optimization design with a width-based score balances coil efficiency against minimum wire width, and a built prototype validates the approach. The optimized coil reaches 2.35-fold efficiency over standard linear coils and cuts spatial variation sharply. It also improves minimum efficiency near the chest wall substantially, with field-map errors under 8 percent.
arxiv-2604-00996: Ferreira and colleagues offer a new take on the chiral-limit pion Bethe-Salpeter equation, solved using state-of-the-art QCD correlation functions as ingredients. The constraints from axial Ward-Takahashi identities hold exactly, both formally and numerically. Bethe-Salpeter equations describe quark binding into mesons, and the chiral limit is the case where light quarks count as massless.
arxiv-2604-01096: Liu and Nagakura present a rough energy-integration method for spotting collisional neutrino flavor instabilities without costly phase-space integrals. Earlier tries mostly assume uniform settings and can go wrong, but the approach keeps the physics of spectral skew and collision rates while yielding a cheap reduced dispersion rule. Tests against exact cases show good results for frequencies and growth rates across even and uneven spreads, for uniform and non-uniform modes. The result is a handy tool for finding such upsets in supernova and neutron-star-merger simulations.
arxiv-2604-01296: Bai and colleagues introduce a bootstrap framework for the representation theory of hidden group symmetries of quantum Hamiltonians, using only a symmetry subgroup and correlations. Their spectral form factor, computed via diagonalization, seeds the bootstrap. Constraints from these data plus fusion rules restrict candidate groups. They recover data: irreducible counts, branching rules, fusion algebra and the character table. The method recovers the Z4 symmetry of the quantum torus chain. It detects projective signatures in a Bose-Hubbard model and the eta-pairing SO(4) symmetry of the Fermi-Hubbard model.
arxiv-2604-01496: Ludwig and colleagues introduce SWE-ZERO to SWE-HERO, a two-stage fine-tuning recipe for SWE-bench distilling frontier language models. SWE-ZERO uses execution-free trajectories to master code semantics and repository reasoning. SWE-HERO applies execution-backed refinement to turn semantic intuitions into rigorous engineering workflows. They release 300k SWE-ZERO and 13k SWE-HERO trajectories from Qwen3-Coder-480B, plus agents. SWE-HERO-32B achieves a 62.2 percent resolution rate on SWE-bench Verified. Despite training only on Python, the agents transfer to SWE-bench Multilingual.
arxiv-2604-01696: Dehler and colleagues tackle the ranked assignment problem in multi-object tracking, where measurements must be matched to tracks to keep self-driving vehicles safe. The number of track guesses grows exponentially, so pruning is essential, and in the delta-GLMB filter that pruning turns into a ranked assignment task. Murty's algorithm and Gibbs sampling handle it with limits on cost or accuracy. Their RAPNet uses bipartite graphs and graph neural networks to model the task, and tests show it beats the Gibbs sampler on accuracy.
arxiv-2604-01896: Hobor and colleagues test whether large language models can act as Bayesian elicitation experts, estimating unknowns. They ask eleven models to estimate population statistics, such as health rates and labor figures, with 95 percent credible intervals, while varying reasoning effort. Larger models give more accurate estimates, but reasoning effort brings no consistent benefit. All models prove overconfident: their intervals contain the true value only 9 to 44 percent of the time. Conformal recalibration expands intervals to intended coverage, and models do well on common topics but struggle with health data.
arxiv-2604-02296: Motamed and colleagues delete objects from video while fixing the physics they disturb. Existing removal tools repaint the background and fix shadows and reflections but fail when removal changes collisions and downstream interactions. VOID trains on paired counterfactual removals built with Kubric and HUMOTO, then uses a vision language model to find affected regions and a video diffusion model to paint consistent outcomes. Tests on synthetic and real clips show steadier scene dynamics after removal than prior methods.
arxiv-2604-02596: Lu and four colleagues test many-shot in-context learning for translating English into ten truly low-resource languages newly added to FLORES+. Giving models more examples helps, but careful example choice matters more: BM25 retrieval makes 50 retrieved examples roughly match 250 ordinary many-shot examples. Retrieved examples also add gains on top of fine-tuning, offering a cheaper path for language communities facing high inference costs.
arxiv-2604-02696: Zhu and three colleagues present VBGS-SLAM, a mapping and localization framework that couples 3D Gaussian splatting with variational Bayesian inference. Rather than optimizing poses deterministically against the splat map, it keeps posterior uncertainty over poses and scene parameters with closed-form updates. The uncertainty-aware design curbs drift and forgetting, giving stronger tracking and high-quality novel view synthesis across synthetic and real scenes.
arxiv-2604-02796: Houdaigoui and Kawarabayashi confirm a conjecture on surface-embeddable graphs. Robertson and Seymour showed in 1990 that such graphs have finitely many minimal excluded minors, but gave no bound. Seymour gave the first general bound in 1993; the authors later reached a quasi-polynomial bound. The new paper proves a polynomial bound. The order of minimal excluded minors for genus g surfaces grows like g squared, up to a small extra factor. The proof swaps a genus bound for a separator bound, using nested contractible cycles.
arxiv-2604-02896: Cheng and six colleagues propose EvaNet, a unified framework for judging infrared and visible image fusion quality. Existing metrics borrowed from other vision tasks miss true fusion quality and cost too much compute. EvaNet uses a lightweight network to approximate widely used metrics. It first splits the fused result into infrared and visible parts, then measures information preservation in each part separately, with contrastive training and language-model scene guidance.
arxiv-2604-03096: Marsal and colleagues built an open navigation system that lets robots drive off road using either LiDAR or a single camera. The camera path predicts depth with a pretrained model, rescales it with sparse motion tracking, and filters false obstacles before building a height map for route planning. In simulated and real rough terrain, the camera setup matched high-resolution LiDAR in most tests.
arxiv-2604-03196: Chowdhury and colleagues test vendor claims that code review agents can handle most pull requests alone, using thousands of real reviewed requests. Agent-only requests merged at 45 percent, 23 points below human-only reviews, and most closed agent-only requests carried very low signal. The team concludes review agents should assist humans rather than replace them, since noisy feedback tracks with abandoned work.
arxiv-2604-03496: Abolhasani and colleagues propose TRACE-KG, a framework that builds a context-enriched knowledge graph and its schema together, without assuming a fixed schema. Conditional links are captured through structured tags, and items and links are ordered by a data-driven schema acting as a reusable meaning scaffold with full trace-back to source evidence. Tests show well-formed, tracked graphs, offering a practical option to fixed-schema and schema-free pipelines.
arxiv-2604-03596: Ithineni and colleagues demonstrate Weyl-like electronic states and chiral transport in SNO/LFO bilayers, tuned by strain and interface design. Transport tests show large non-saturating MR, a bent Hall response, and a chiral quirk under parallel fields. First-principles math reveals a doubled Weyl semimetallic phase guarded by screw axis pattern, driven by edge lattice bends.
arxiv-2604-03696: Zhengyu Fu and colleagues built FunFact, a system that maps what objects in a 3D scene are for, not just where they sit. It first charts objects and parts from posed color-and-depth images, proposes plausible functional links, then settles all links jointly with a factor graph using common-sense and geometric priors. Tests on three scene collections improved discovery recall and confidence calibration.
arxiv-2604-03896: Yoshiyuki Ootani proposed a graduated trust gate for IoT location checks, replacing a blunt accept-or-reject verdict. The gate scores several integrity signals and chooses PROCEED, STEP-UP, or DENY, with step-up calling a stronger verifier like a zero-knowledge proximity proof. A session latch blocks the whole session after one suspicious fix, stopping score recovery. On 10,000 synthetic traces, strict thresholds kept false denies at zero where a binary gate still denied some honest users.
arxiv-2604-04296: Klazar presents Thomassen's proof and Filippov's proof of the Weak Jordan Theorem, each in full detail with modern rigour. The theorem states that the complement of any topological circuit in the plane is disconnected. In plain terms, a closed loop drawn in the plane splits the plane into separate pieces. The paper sets out both arguments side by side, letting readers compare how each proof reaches the same split.
arxiv-2604-04696: Ji and five colleagues present GPIR, a GPU-accelerated private information retrieval system rethinking kernel design, data layout and scheduling. GPUs suit these tasks with batching, yet batching expands working sets beyond L2 cache capacity. GPIR introduces a stage-aware hybrid model switching between operation-level and stage-level kernels fusing operations into one kernel. For RowSel, a transposed layout with fine-grained pipelining resolves the layout mismatch for tiled multiplications. GPIR extends to multi-GPU systems, scaling throughput and capacity, reaching up to 297.2x higher throughput than PIRonGPU.
arxiv-2604-05096: Liu, Cao, and Li study the limits of language model adaptation under knowledge drift in the real world. Large language models acquire knowledge during pretraining, tying them to a snapshot of the world. As facts, entities, and events change, models may suffer outdated predictions and inconsistent reasoning. Existing approaches such as fine-tuning, knowledge editing, and retrieval-augmented generation aim to update model knowledge. Yet they are rarely evaluated on evolving knowledge. The authors introduce a benchmark of dynamic events to test adaptation under drift.
arxiv-2604-05196: Xing and three colleagues study checks on Friedkin-Johnsen opinion shifts from binary reads. Each opinion is cut at a threshold. The goal is to check whether a model with given firmness settings and initial views can make the seen outputs. The model is framed as a step system, with matching defined by nearness of paths and outputs. A set of models, built by trimming the influence matrix and splitting settings and initial views, covers any model and is itself covered by a model, giving finite checks.
arxiv-2604-05296: George and three colleagues take a view of embeddings powering search systems, constrained by unmeasured identity leakage on face data and no fixes. They contribute a benchmark checking at low rates, a template inversion check, and attribution with perturbations. They propose a projector removing an identity subspace while keeping utility space, called ISP. Across two datasets, encoders prove robust, with CLIP leaking more than DINO and SSCD and resisting inversion. ISP drives access to chance while keeping utility, transfers well, and shows subspace removal achieves privacy with utility preserved.
arxiv-2604-05396: Liu and nine colleagues test whether demonstrations from other fields can improve in-context learning when expert examples are missing, a companion question to retrieval design. Their experiments find conditional positive transfer: past an example absorption threshold, added demonstrations more often help, and gains grow. Analysis traces the benefit to repair of reasoning structure by retrieved examples rather than to shared surface meaning.
arxiv-2604-05796: Kepič and three colleagues steer phase flips in vanadium dioxide nanocylinders via patterning, crystallization, and dewetting. The fast near-room switch with hysteresis suits short-term memory and brain-like computing, but device use was limited to films. Shaped nano-builds on chips open scalable energy-saving memory and neuromorphic photonics.
arxiv-2604-05996: In a 2026 search, the CMS Collaboration hunts for a Higgs boson made alongside a W or Z boson. The boson would break apart into a soft unclustered energy pattern, a spray of many slow charged particles. The team uses proton-proton collision data gathered at the LHC from 2016 to 2018, equal to 138 inverse femtobarns. It examines final states with a leptonic W or Z decay for the first time. No signal rises above background, so the paper limits such Higgs decays across the model's parameter range.
arxiv-2604-06196: Huang and four colleagues tackle three-way logical question answering, where a hypothesis earns True, False, or Unknown given premises. Models fail when answers to a hypothesis and its negation break the label mapping, or when the model abstains with Unknown though one side follows. Their CGD-PD layer, training-free at test time, combines neural classification with symbolic negation-consistency projection and entailment probes. On a FOLIO split it gains up to 6.8 points on Claude Sonnet, while cutting Unknown predictions, in a proof of concept only.
arxiv-2604-06296: Hua and six colleagues introduce AgentOpt, the first framework-agnostic package for client-side optimization of language-model agents. Server-side work targets caching and load balancing, while client-side optimization spreads model choice, tools, and API budget across stages under quality, cost, and latency limits. The report first studies model selection, assigning models to roles, where best and worst differ in cost by 13 to 32 times at matched accuracy. AgentOpt offers ten search algorithms; across four benchmarks, UCB-E recovers top accuracy while cutting budget 62 to 76 percent over brute force.
arxiv-2604-06396: Ortega and Arribillaga ask which priority violations are justifiable when making Deferred Acceptance, the standard school method, more efficient. A violation is justifiable, they argue, when the hurt student either gains from the change that caused it or cannot improve under any assignment that Pareto-dominates it. Their just-below-cutoffs method always finds such a change whenever its outcome wastes potential, and iterating it reaches a matching no justifiable outcome can Pareto-improve. Data and simulations show how far justifiability and consent limits block Pareto-efficient outcomes.
arxiv-2604-06596: Shovan and four colleagues speed up label propagation when graph data arrives in batches. Instead of relabeling the whole graph each time, their GPU-centered method, DynLP, updates only the affected subgraph, propagating changes where needed without full recalculation. Built on graphics-processor optimizations, it ran on average 13 times faster than leading methods on large datasets. At best it ran up to 102 times faster, offering a practical update path for semi-supervised learning on growing graphs.
arxiv-2604-06796: Pollastro and three colleagues narrow the amortization gap in variational autoencoders. Shared encoder settings make posterior fitting cheap but leave a gap versus per-instance inference. Their IA-VAE adds a hypernetwork that tunes a shared encoder per input, adapting it within a single forward pass. Theory shows the IA-VAE family contains standard amortized methods, so its best bound cannot worsen. Tests on synthetic data with known posteriors and on image benchmarks show more accurate fits and better held-out bounds with far fewer weights.
arxiv-2604-06896: Pasqui and nine colleagues build VertAX, a fast physics engine that learns settings for cell mechanics. Cell sheets reshape through local pushes between cells, which vertex models capture, yet many settings make fitting hard. VertAX adds auto-diff and GPU speed for forward runs, fits, and inverse design, plus user energy and cost functions. Demos on tissue growth, fits, and inverse design show its strength. A benchmark finds equilibrium propagation can gauge gradients from repeated forward runs alone, opening inverse problems to sim tools without learning.
arxiv-2604-06996: Pombal, Rei, and Martins present the first study of self-preference bias in rubric-based evaluation. Judges favor their own outputs or model family, skewing development, especially for self-improvement. Using IFEval and LiveCodeBench, benchmarks with verifiable rubrics, bias persists even when criteria are objective. Where generators fail, judges are over 50 percent more likely to wrongly pass their own outputs. Ensembling judges mitigates bias but does not eliminate it. On HealthBench, a medical benchmark with subjective rubrics, bias skews scores by up to 10 points, decisive when ranking models.
arxiv-2604-07196: Lee probes whether Evo2, a DNA language model that reads million-token stretches, has actually learned the three-dimensional folding of chromosomes. Using tests on domain boundaries and convergent CTCF loops, he finds the model cannot tell functional changes from matched random ones and only partly recovers boundaries. The verdict is that Evo2 knows local CTCF patterns but misses higher-order folding, pointing future work toward architectures that fold in cell type and contact data.
arxiv-2604-07396: Zhang and Fong propose SHIELD, a split memory design for thrifty language-model inference on edge neural processing units. On-chip memory is scarce, and refreshing embedded DRAM workspaces burns much energy. SHIELD splits bfloat16 activations by field, separating sign and exponent bits from mantissa bits. It skips refresh for short-lived query and attention-output mantissas and eases refresh for long-lived key-value mantissas. Across models and settings, SHIELD cuts refresh energy by 35 percent while holding accuracy on WikiText-2, PIQA, plus ARC-Easy.
arxiv-2604-07496: Huvar, Jonáš, and Pastva tackle model inference for biological systems with uninterpreted functions plus monotonicity constraints, which force certain inputs to push outputs consistently up or down. They compare naive quantified encodings against eager quantifier instantiation, which uses a finite collection of quantifier-free monotonicity lemmas, plus a lazy variant that adds lemmas on demand. On a large systems-biology benchmark set, instantiation-based encodings beat quantified ones, which struggle with large arities and complex cases. The SMT approach also beats leading domain tools Bonesis and AEON.
arxiv-2604-07896: Tanner, Kam, and Wang review non-variational labeled quantum kernel methods for quantum machine learning. Unlike variational methods, which rely on gradient-based tuning and can suffer barren plateaus, non-variational methods use fixed quantum feature maps. Model choice then proceeds on classical hardware through convex optimization and cross-validation. Splitting quantum feature coding from classical training keeps tuning stable while quantum circuits encode data in large Hilbert spaces. The review covers classical kernel basics, fidelity and projected kernel designs, practical gauging methods, and ways to judge quantum edge.
arxiv-2604-07996: Karbstein derives the leading cold correction to the Heisenberg-Euler Lagrangian in a constant electromagnetic field at two loops from its one-loop zero-temperature twin. Using the real-time formalism of equilibrium quantum field theory, which separates zero-temperature parts from finite-temperature fixes, the determination becomes nearly trivial. It requires only derivatives of the one-loop cold Lagrangian with respect to field strength. As a bonus, one-particle reducible tadpole structures dress the two-loop cold contribution, generating a subset of higher-loop contributions in the cold limit.
arxiv-2604-08096: Yazdi discusses the Thurston norm and the Euler class on compact 3-manifolds. Thurston's norm on second homology determines by duality a dual norm on second cohomology. Thurston asked whether whole-number edge points of the dual norm ball carry a geometric meaning. Thurston showed the Euler class of any taut foliation's oriented tangent plane field lies in the dual unit ball. He guessed every whole-number edge point appears as such a class. The chapter surveys shape, topological, and motion-based forms giving such points and the guess's status.
arxiv-2604-08196: Agrawal presents a statistical-AI framework for finding flares in SDSS Stripe 82 quasar light curves. Quasars vary by chance across wavelengths, usually matching Damped Random Walk. They show extreme luminosity changes, called flares, departing sharply from normal pattern and probing accretion disc motion and giant black hole fuel. Although modern transient surveys spurred buzz in flares, nobody has searched the legacy SDSS Stripe 82 set, which holds 9,258 quasars watched over roughly 10 years. The main challenge is telling rare events apart from ever-present random shifts.
arxiv-2604-08996: Heiden and eight colleagues show how to control phonon polaritons, trapped light waves in layered crystals, by shaping the substrate beneath them. Today's substrate patterning is binary and gives limited control over the polariton wavelength, though geometry, isotope mix, and nearby matter can shift it. Their platform tunes the wavelength locally in hexagonal boron nitride, squeezes it and stretches it back, and funnels the waves by a factor of about 2.5 by geometry alone. The result pushes substrate engineering forward and offers local control of polaritonic modes.
arxiv-2604-09196: Dong, Wang, and Ma improve quantum state transfer through a three-level system by slowly following a dark state. In real multilevel systems, control pulses leak into extra levels and cap transfer quality. The authors model that leakage and use Pontryagin's principle to design penalized controls within realistic Gaussian pulse shapes. Simulations on a transmon platform show higher fidelity and stronger tolerance to amplitude errors and detuning drift.
arxiv-2604-09496: Ohm studies a nonlocal curve evolution for an inextensible elastic filament moving in a three-dimensional Stokes fluid. The model captures the main part of a full free-boundary problem, with fluid effects packed into a pseudodifferential force-to-velocity operator. That operator sits between resistive force theory for long waves and a Stokes boundary-value problem for short ones. Ohm proves global well-posedness in the natural energy space and shows resistive force theory emerging as the filament radius shrinks to zero.
arxiv-2604-09696: Nicholson studies Sharpness-Aware Surrogate Training for on-sensor spiking networks, where smooth models degrade at deployment under a hard threshold. Sharpness-aware minimization on a surrogate-forward network keeps training smooth and gradients exact. Contraction assumptions yield state-stability, input-Lipschitz, and smoothness bounds plus a nonconvex convergence result. On event-camera benchmarks, hard-spike accuracy under swap-only conditions rises sharply. N-MNIST climbs from about 66 to about 95 percent, and DVS Gesture from about 32 to about 63 percent. Quantized-weight simulations preserve gains, and synaptic operations fall.
arxiv-2604-09796: Banerjee and four co-authors show resist-free Josephson junction making based on etched silicon trenches. The polymer mask in resist-based schemes causes dirt and limits surface prep, junction metals, and scale-up. Their method fits CMOS and joins current base-layer making and wet steps. They make aluminum-aluminum oxide-aluminum junctions and qubits, with median energy decay times up to 184 millionths of a second. Dirt at the substrate-metal edge proves minimal, and energy-decay shifts over 35 hours run narrow and bell-shaped.
arxiv-2604-09896: Deangelis, Focardi, and Zeppieri prove random blending for curved far problems with many small random blocks. The model case is a Dirichlet fractional p problem, with answers pinned to zero on small random balls. The balls come from a marked point process, with clumping. Under moment rules on radii, the fractional p-room density is adding almost surely at edge scaling. This yields a real blended problem like regular or well-apart cases. The analysis extends to shaped blocks and broad far kernels, via a smooth Palm-measure proof.
arxiv-2604-10496: Yin and seven colleagues tame wild values that wreck low precision expert models. Under post training quantization, stray magnitudes drive large errors in mixture of experts nets. Their CodeQuant scheme smooths activations with learnable turns and parks weight strays in tuned cluster centers. A matched kernel plan for graphics and central chips seals the design. It runs over four times faster while beating top quantization rivals on varied expert models.
arxiv-2604-10896: Hewage, Chakkravarthy, and Abeysekara link Born-rule stats from variational circuits to Bayesian posterior uncertainty, proving quantum measures yield calibrated intervals with no Bayesian gear. On residual circuits, shot-based uncertainty lands coverage within 1 to 3 percent at 5,000 or more, while Monte Carlo dropout over-covers by 4 to 5 percent. Constrained circuits cut calibration error by 34 to 40 percent versus unconstrained peers, with intervals 14 to 30 percent narrower at coverage. Quantum circuits draw 15 percent more facts than Monte Carlo dropout and 42 percent more than ensembles, via the exponential Hilbert space of Born-rule sampling.
arxiv-2604-10996: Yang asks whether language models can generate numerical features for reinforcement learning trading agents. He builds a pipeline where a frozen language model extracts features, turning daily news and filings into a vector for a PPO agent. A prompt loop tunes extraction against the information coefficient, the rank link between predicted and realized returns. The tuned prompt finds predictive features. Yet during an economy-wide shock, the language-model features add noise and the agent trails a price-only baseline. Economy-wide state variables stay the most robust driver.
arxiv-2604-11296: Luz and Carloni introduce new generating theorems in general relativity for anisotropic, static, spherically symmetric solutions of Einstein's equations. The theorems yield a class of interior models for compact stars. Their shape and thermal properties are studied in detail, with some new spacetimes holding known solutions as special cases. In short, one recipe now yields many star interiors, old and new, from a single starting point. A constant-density solution is assessed as a candidate for the incompressible limit of compact stars against the Bowers-Liang spacetime.
arxiv-2604-11496: Miranda and three colleagues revisit composition in dual vision models: the block may be inference, not features. Dual encoders like CLIP look like bag-of-words systems on composition benchmarks. Enforcing fine region matching at inference sharply improves composition performance without updating encoders. The authors then train a model to learn such matchings from frozen patch and token vectors. Learning localized matching over frozen features matches full fine-tuning on domain retrieval. It also improves outside composition benchmarks. Full fine-tuning and prior composition training fail to transfer under shift.
arxiv-2604-11896: Bianchi and four colleagues give a strong-coupling account of defect renormalization-group flows in ABJM theory via holography. Wilson loop operators anchor the study; string fluctuations around AdS2 backgrounds map worldsheet excitations to dual defect operators, fixing their scaling dimensions with one-loop terms. Boundary conditions on string coordinates yield distinct cases and a geometric picture of flows through interpolating choices. The half-BPS loop proves infrared stable, the sixth-BPS loop acts as a saddle point, and the non-supersymmetric setup emerges as a natural ultraviolet fixed point.
arxiv-2604-11996: Pathak and four colleagues argue that benchmark accuracy alone cannot reveal thinking quality, since models can reach right answers through flawed thinking or rote memory. They propose a score rating traces on faithfulness, coherence, utility, and factuality. Lumping all traces misleads, above all over long runs where shaky correct traces may be luck. Their Filtered Reasoning Score instead uses only the top-K percent surest traces. Models tied on accuracy then differ sharply on thinking quality, and higher scores predict better results on other benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-12496: Ryo Sawada and two colleagues test whether supernova SN 2023uqf could power a cosmic particle accelerator. The blast arrived close in time and direction to a 442 TeV IceCube alert. One-dimensional simulations match the observed light curves with a dense helium-rich shell. That shell's density falls with radius to the power of minus three. Shock physics then opens a short window for multi-PeV particle acceleration. Hadronic collisions in that window could yield neutrinos. The alert's timing and energy fit the window, though one event cannot prove the link.
arxiv-2604-12596: Valter Hudovernik and six colleagues scale foundation models for relational learning. KumoRFM-2 works on linked tables directly, without manual flattening. It preserves temporal consistency while handling one or more tables at once. Pre-training spans row, column, foreign key, and cross-sample axes. Task information enters early, sharpening column selection and noise robustness. Tests on 41 benchmarks show gains up to 8 percent over supervised and foundation rivals. Few-shot performance already beats supervised methods on common tasks. The model scales to billion-scale relational datasets.
arxiv-2604-12696: Daniel Albert presents a dynamic parallel constant-time algorithm for longest common extension queries. An LCE query finds the longest shared prefix or suffix at two positions. The structure supports character insertions and deletions. It runs on a common CRCW PRAM with work scaling as n to a small power. A synchronizing sets hierarchy answers substring equality queries. Those answers feed LCE queries. Stored information may lag by up to log n log-star n updates. Two applications follow: Dyck language membership and square maintenance.
arxiv-2604-12796: Indranil Biswas and four colleagues use complex tests to concentrate entanglement. Imaginarity saves resources in optical setups. In three-qubit assistance, complex bases boost bipartite entanglement with a third party's aid. A modified swapping protocol uses a symmetric complex basis that beats the standard GHZ basis. A weaker basis beats a maximal one at making entanglement. The construction also answers open problems from 2023. On a honeycomb lattice, it cuts per-bond entanglement need by 10.6 percent and bond need by about 23 percent.
arxiv-2604-12896: Muhammad Kamran Janjua and three colleagues rewrite vision tool outputs as language-native summaries. Dense pixel outputs clash with language reasoning strengths, so tools often fail to help. Perception Programs turn tool outputs into compact structured summaries models can parse. On six BLINK tasks, the method lifts base models and raw tool baselines. With GPT-5 Mini, multi-view reasoning jumps from 41.35 percent to 86.47 percent. Relative depth rises from about 52 percent to about 81 percent. Average gains reach 22 percent, with smaller models gaining 15 to 40 points.
arxiv-2604-12996: Nicaise, Bermudez, and Perlaza prove that two optimal transport problems, each penalized by a different divergence measure, can share the same unique solution. The link holds when the transport cost is transformed in a matching way, within spaces with bounded costs. The result ties together families of regularized transport problems that had looked distinct, showing their solutions coincide under the right cost change.
arxiv-2604-13096: Cintio, Michelangeli, and Tsutskov propose exactly solvable models of quantum reinforcement learning built on a unitary-control-then-measure protocol, where an agent transforms a quantum state and interleaves each step with a projective measurement. They derive closed-form trajectory probabilities, rewards, and expected returns for four concrete realizations. Complexity of the expected return drops from exponential in trajectory length to a power law. Optimal policies show Zeno-governed unique optima in low-dimensional models but plateau and discrete degeneracy in the four-level system.
arxiv-2604-13396: Vakhnovskyi presents HierFedCEA, a shared-learning setup for climate control across indoor farms that keep their raw data private. Shared learning across farms can cut HVAC energy by 30 to 38 percent, but grow recipes are trade secrets. It splits a compact 36-parameter PID tuning model into three tiers: global physics, crop groups, and local tweaks, each with its own privacy budget. Simulations based on years of farm data reach 94 percent of central training scores while sending under 1 megabyte.
arxiv-2604-13796: Padalkar designs a ranking engine for daily fantasy sports, where users must pick matches in a narrow window before games lock. Static recommenders handle deadlines poorly. His engine adapts the Deep Interest Network by injecting temporality at two levels: urgency features computed live for each candidate match, and temporal positional encodings that weigh past actions by recency. A listwise neuralNDCG loss produces urgency-aware rankings. Trained across multiple nodes and GPUs on over 650,000 users and 100 billion interactions, it lifts nDCG at rank one by 9 percent over a tuned LightGBM baseline.
arxiv-2604-14096: Perrinet builds working memory into a recurrent spiking network by giving each synapse 41 heterogeneous delays. Target spike patterns become chains of overlapping spiking motifs, windows that predict the next spike. On a synthetic benchmark of 16 patterns over 512 neurons and 1000 steps, training reaches a perfect F1 score, with recall spreading forward from the clamped starting window. Heterogeneous delays thus offer an efficient substrate for neuromorphic edge memory.
arxiv-2604-14296: Lee and nine colleagues introduce the dynamic compass code, a subsystem scheme with a fresh syndrome extraction cycle for heavy-hex qubit arrays. A distance-5 device built from superconducting qubits tests the code, while averaged circuit eigenvalue sampling maps fine, context-dependent errors across syndrome extraction. Soft measurement information feeds the decoder with measurement error data and flags leakage for exclusion by post-selection. The noise-informed approach cuts the logical error rate by up to 38.3 percent on the distance-5 device.
arxiv-2604-14696: Saito, Kishimoto, and Tanaka built a trial system that reads high-energy physics papers, extracts their event-selection rules, and turns them into runnable code. Tested on a published ATLAS Higgs search in four-lepton events from 2015 and 2016 open data, it recovered many documented cuts and sometimes matched a hand-written baseline exactly. Randomness, invented details, and failed runs still limit it, so they present it as a supervised aid, not an autonomous analyst.
arxiv-2604-14796: Uludoğan, Giledereli, Ozkirimli, and Özgür introduce PUFFIN, a framework that finds protein units, groups of residues between single residues and whole proteins in scale. It treats proteins as residue-level structure graphs and applies a graph neural network with structure-aware pooling, shaped by functional supervision. The learned units prove structurally coherent, show organized links to molecular function, and match curated InterPro annotations in meaningful ways. PUFFIN thus gives an interpretable route into structure-function links, with code public.
arxiv-2604-14896: Sumyk and Kosovan present an early investigation of agentic retrieval-augmented generation for Ukrainian, built for the UNLP 2026 shared task on multi-domain document understanding. Their system pairs two-stage retrieval, BGE-M3 with BGE reranking, with a light agentic layer that rephrases queries and retries answers atop Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct. Retrieval quality proves the main bottleneck: agentic retries lift answer accuracy, but overall scores stay capped by document and page identification. They discuss offline pipeline limits and point toward stronger retrieval joined with more advanced agentic reasoning for Ukrainian.
arxiv-2604-15096: Böhi and colleagues build a heart-imaging model that learns across views instead of treating each frame alone. Standard masked autoencoders handle images or short clips apart, missing the multi-view structure of echocardiograms. Their LAMAE model adds latent attention so frames and views exchange information directly, rebuilding a fuller picture of cardiac function from partial views. Pretrained on a large real-world echo dataset, it also predicts ICD-10 codes and transfers from adult to child cases.
arxiv-2604-15296: Terradot and Danos ask why all cells share a common ionic logic for holding intracellular pH steady yet use wildly different transporter toolkits. They derive a thermodynamic floor on the power needed to maintain ionic motive forces, equal to the energy lost through ion leakage. Minimizing cost recovers the universal potassium-rich, sodium-poor cytoplasm from membrane permeability alone, and explains why extreme settings push cells toward new metabolic regimes.
arxiv-2604-15396: González and Negrín present a new route to the Riemann Hypothesis in a short note. They show it equivalent to a statement built on the Salem integral equation. The note thus reframes the famous unsolved hypothesis as a question about that integral equation, giving researchers another angle from which to attack it.
arxiv-2604-15496: Maggiore builds a six-dimensional, Maxwell-like fracton theory that stays covariant, using a tensor gauge field that is symmetric and has scalar gauge symmetry. In this relativistic frame, limited mobility follows at once from gauge invariance and the allowed couplings to matter. He constructs the stress-energy tensor, whose trace has one dimension-set shape that turns into a total derivative in six dimensions. Charge-plus-dipole conservation then pins lone charges in place while dipolar pairs stay mobile.
arxiv-2604-15596: Jacobsen and Kohli study aid allocation under differential privacy, asking how privacy, efficiency, and targeting precision trade off. Person-level targeting faces both utility doubts, since simple unit-level plans can match it, and privacy objections, leaving unit-level targeting urged on both grounds. Studying private versions of both plans across random and distribution-free settings, they derive clean bounds on the three-way trade-off under varied data limits.
arxiv-2604-15696: Skowronek and four colleagues build tests and gauges for the stability index of symmetric stable laws, in one and two dims, from a tweaked Greenwood stat. The stat, first made for plus-only data, here gets a two-dim form, with a close look at the sub-Gaussian case and two test variants. In one dim, the same attack gauges the index. Sims show it beats old ways and tells Gaussian laws from near-Gaussian stable laws with an index near 2.
arxiv-2604-15896: Zhang and Akan study signal detection for mobile molecular links with counting receivers, where movement makes sender-receiver geometry uncertain. Motion and geometry shifts scramble signal strength and add spread beyond plain Poisson noise. They propose a profiled dispersion-domain statistic that removes the plain Poisson part and scales by the squared mean shape, aiming for stable thresholds under multiplicative gain. Simulations with active-Brownian motion and finite-memory interference support the design, showing threshold stability where mean differences are weak or suppressed.
arxiv-2604-16096: N. C. Combe shows the Hilbert space of Koopman-von Neumann Landau-Ginzburg theory is parametrized by a Monge-Ampère domain with pre-Frobenius structure. For finite exponential families, the parameter space becomes such a domain and manifold. The theorem proves that for every Berglund-Hübsch-Krawitz mirror pair of Calabi-Yau orbifolds, this domain, the open simplex, bases a Lagrangian torus fibration on both hypersurfaces, with dual fibres in the SYZ sense. This proves the Kontsevich-Soibelman conjecture for all such mirror pairs.
arxiv-2604-16196: Murakami and 12 colleagues analyse XRISM and NuSTAR data on NGC 7213, a nearby active galactic nucleus feeding at a low rate. They test whether its highly ionized iron lines come from photoionization or collisional ionization. Fits to two iron lines hint at different velocity widths, and they test one-zone and two-zone models for each process against the broad energy data.
arxiv-2604-16296: Hultgren and Khalid construct bases that are valuatively independent for the Fermat family of cubic curves. For each k at least 1, they build a basis for line-bundle powers, from sections in projective space. They give a formula for canonical tropical theta functions and the cost function for any such bases. They show the tropical theta functions solve a real Monge-Ampère operator, while the cost function reflects monodromy of a Hessian structure on the skeleton. Notably, both differ from versions induced by monomial or ambient projective bases.
arxiv-2604-16596: Armadillo and colleagues project future rings' reach for new physics through exact SM tests. Focus falls on electron sites: FCC-ee, LEP and LCF. Reads run through Higgs link shifts, Higgs and weak-force links, and global SMEFT fits. The SMEFT study adds running flow, linear and squared terms, and higher-order cross fixes. Matching to full models, they gauge reach to mixed Higgs models and single Standard Model add-ons. They release an updated open SMEFiT tool so results can be rerun, grown and tuned.
arxiv-2604-16796: Tang and Yang propose ADDPS, a diffusion receiver using switching dual-domain posterior sampling. Gen meaning communication uses ready priors to improve perceptual quality of radio image sending. Old boxes rely on MAP estimation, which cannot keep the data distribution. Single-domain guidance fails twice: latent-domain guidance is touchy to channel noise, while image-domain guidance gets decoder bias. Alternating latent-domain and image-domain match splits joint sampling into simpler parts, dodging gradient conflicts. On FFHQ, ADDPS hits top look quality over older methods.
arxiv-2604-17296: Linnebo presents the view that objects are made step by step in an endless process, with truths settled step by step. Two modes analyze the view: object making and truth settling, yielding a standard bimodal logic. Mirror theorems give simpler theories by switching off one or both modes for a less standard logic. Switching off object making yields a narrow plural logic, while switching off truth settling yields a weaker logic. The approach is shown with a Weyl-style set theory, Cantor's domain principle, and the view about Cantor sets.
arxiv-2604-17396: Xiao and colleagues tackle machine unlearning: making a language model forget sensitive or harmful material without harming what it should keep. Their method REGLU starts low-rank adapters in a representation-guided subspace and forces updates into the orthogonal complement of the kept material's subspace. This sidesteps parameter-importance scores, which fail because single parameters serve many uses at once. On two unlearning benchmarks it beat leading baselines, forgetting more cleanly while keeping model utility high.
arxiv-2604-17496: Malami sheds new light on the B-to-pi-K puzzle, a testing ground for the Standard Model and CP violation. The key channel is the neutral B decay to a neutral pion and a neutral kaon, the only mode showing direct CP violation together with mixing-induced CP violation. Fresh Belle II data on its CP asymmetries feed an updated analysis with new insight into the long-standing puzzle. Looking ahead to a high-precision era, the system may yet reveal new sources of CP violation.
arxiv-2604-17696: Feng and eleven colleagues present STRATAGEM, which learns transferable thought through path-tuned game self-play in language models. Old self-play uses only end-game results, failing to split transferable thought patterns from game-only tricks. STRATAGEM rewards paths showing abstract, domain-free thought through a transfer score, and rewards adaptive thought growth via an evolution reward. Tests across math, general reasoning, and code benchmarks show strong gains, most on contest math, with cut-out tests and human review backing both parts.
arxiv-2604-18196: Dinu, Vermetten, and Doerr tackle algorithm selection for black-box optimization, where the goal is hidden and only outputs can be probed. Picking a single algorithm risks a bad choice from selector error or unlucky variance. They therefore split the evaluation budget across a portfolio of algorithms, which cuts variance and exploits complementary strengths. A simple portfolio over the full training set already beats the virtual best solver, and a nearest-neighbor refinement for unseen instances improves it further.
arxiv-2604-18596: Affonso shows language models as self-run bargaining, teaming, and vying agents develop game habits. Across 51,906 trials from 25 models, rivalry and teamwork converge while teaming splits 48-fold from about 2 to about 72 percent. Maker name best predicts teaming, and the split is unstable across versions: OpenAI fell from about 50 to about 2 percent while Google rose from about 8 to about 57 percent. Anthropic frontier models sustain 57 percent teaming in the final round of repeat games, while newest Google models team up throughout but defect when penalty ends.
arxiv-2604-18796: Çakır and Mutuk investigate triply heavy baryons omega-ccb and omega-cbb: their mass spectra, magnetic moments, and Regge trajectories. They use a nonrelativistic quark-diquark model, reducing the three body problem to a two body system. The Bc meson spectrum sets the parameters. Ground masses are about 8 GeV for omega-ccb and about 11 GeV for omega-cbb, with excitation patterns matching the literature. Magnetic moments for spin one half and three half states match other approaches, and Regge slopes scale with heavy quark content.
arxiv-2604-18996: Pocklington and Clerk present an exact technique for matchgate observables under arbitrary Pauli noise. They use it on critical ground states, focusing on the 1D transverse field Ising model under Markovian noise. Such noise cannot kill critical spin correlations, yet it yields a nonequilibrium state with signatures needing no postselection or copies. Despite infinite temperature dissipation, the state shows a thermal spread of low energy quasiparticles from a noise induced scale. The effects are reachable with a single probe qubit, and the results hold for a dephased XX chain state.
arxiv-2604-19296: Hess, Frauen, Kilbertus, and Feuerriegel introduce DOPE, a debiased neural operator for estimating summary quantities of physical system trajectories. Often the goal is not the full trajectory but a single target number, like time spent in a range, time above a threshold, accumulated cost, or total energy. Naive plug-in estimation from neural operators can suffer first-order bias. DOPE corrects that bias, works with partial and irregular observations, and pairs with any neural operator design.
arxiv-2604-19396: Zhang and colleagues test whether big science facilities yield more novel and interdisciplinary knowledge, a claim rarely checked with data. They gather 310,086 publications from 88 global facilities and build a matched control set of about 3 million publications sharing the same last authors. The study measures whether facility use actually drives innovation beyond comparable work without them, after decades of massive investment in advanced tools and platforms. Facility-linked work is then compared against the matched controls on novelty and interdisciplinarity.
arxiv-2604-19496: Xiao, Li, and Shen propose EvoPatch-IoT, a retrieval framework for stripped BusyBox firmware binaries across architectures. BusyBox is widely reused in Linux-based Internet-of-Things firmware. Security assessment stays hard because images are stripped and vendor patch practices vary. EvoPatch-IoT combines anonymous instruction features, graph statistics, geometric priors, and historical prototypes to find vulnerable functions without symbols or version strings. The work targets a part found in countless home and factory devices. Its tests need no source code and no version labels.
arxiv-2604-19596: Maboudi and colleagues present PC2Model, an ISPRS benchmark on 3D point cloud to model registration. Registration aligns one point cloud with another or with a 3D model, merging multimodal data into one representation. That skill is essential for construction monitoring, autonomous driving, robotics, and virtual or augmented reality. As point cloud capture tools like LiDAR and structured light scanning grow more accessible, research focus has shifted to downstream tasks. Point cloud-to-model registration leads that shift, though data-driven methods still struggle with sparsity, noise, clutter, and occlusions.
arxiv-2604-19696: Gundhi, Infantino, and Bassi challenge a recent Nature paper claiming quantum particles become entangled through classical gravity. They show the claimed entanglement follows from letting particles diffuse between objects. It vanishes when diffusion is barred, since the wavefunction stays in separate parts. Because entanglement depends on the chosen split of Hilbert space, they argue free evolution is what entangles, not the classical pull. This holds even with no interaction pull present.
arxiv-2604-19796: Castillo Pereda extends the Gai-Kapadia framework, built for bank contagion, to systemic risk and default cascades in global equity markets. The study analyzes a 30-asset network of equities over 2015 to 2026, building networks from price moves and filtering for significant links. Cascade dynamics are tested with fixed propagation and Monte Carlo simulations under varying shocks. Results show strong global resilience and a tiny chance of large-scale failure, plus localized vulnerability.
arxiv-2604-20296: Xu, Lu, and Song take survival analysis online under the Cox proportional hazards model, where treatment choices must adapt as new data arrive. They face staggered entry, delayed feedback, and right censoring, adapting three classic bandit methods to balance exploration and exploitation. Theory gives sublinear regret bounds for the adapted methods. Simulations and semi-real tests on SEER cancer data show fast effective learning of near-optimal treatment policies.
arxiv-2604-20496: Blain responds to the April 2026 Claude Mythos sandbox escape, which Anthropic has not publicly explained. He treats the suspected arithmetic flaw as an unverified class, not a confirmed cause, and presents COBALT, a Z3 checker. It hunts arithmetic flaw patterns in C and C++ infrastructure before deployment. Validated on NASA cFE, wolfSSL, Eclipse Mosquitto, and NASA F Prime, it gives concrete witnesses for flaws and guarantees within stated bounds. Blain pairs it with a four-layer containment plan covering checking, pre-execution limits, output control, and monitoring.
arxiv-2604-20996: Belay and colleagues build language-tutoring resources for African languages that lack training data. They start from AFRILANGDICT, a collection of 194,700 African language-English dictionary entries, and use it to generate AFRILANGEDU, a set of 78,900 multi-turn student-tutor examples for supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization. Tutors trained on it across 10 African languages beat their base models, and combining the two training stages brings gains from about 2 to about 16 percent under judge-based scoring.
arxiv-2604-21396: Byeonggeuk Lim and three colleagues make vision-language reasoning trustworthy by tying each reasoning step to real visual evidence. Their VG-CoT dataset links steps to image regions through a fully automated three-stage pipeline. Detection and OCR extract object- and text-level evidence, GPT-4o generates grounded step-by-step reasoning, and rationale-driven open-set detection refines the grounding. A new benchmark scores rationale quality, answer accuracy, and reasoning-answer alignment. Tests on LLaVA-1.5 and Qwen2-VL show consistent gains on most metrics.
arxiv-2604-21596: František Bartoš and three colleagues recover Bayes factor sensitivity curves from one model fit, instead of refitting per value. Each Bayes factor splits into an anchor value and a Savage-Dickey ratio from an extended hyper-prior model. Each value follows from the anchor and posterior density ordinates, estimated by importance weighting. Because the parameter enters only through the prior, the likelihood cancels, leaving prior evaluations on MCMC draws. The estimator is fast, accurate on samples, beats kernel density estimation, and extends to multiple parameters and model averaging.
arxiv-2604-21696: Vogel and five colleagues introduce TEmBed, a unified test bed for tabular foundation models, which aim to learn reusable representations of table data for retrieval, search, and prediction. Existing models are hard to compare because each is tested under its own task settings. TEmBed evaluates embeddings at cell, row, column, and table level, showing that the best model depends on the task and level, and offering practical guidance for choosing one.
arxiv-2604-21796: Li and ten colleagues design a new precursor to build a gulf-edged chiral graphene nanoribbon with atomic precision on a gold surface. Microscope images confirm the exact ribbon structure. Light spectra and theory identify a closed-shell semiconducting state with a band gap of 1.8 electron volts. Raman work resolves a vibration mode sitting at the gulf-edge carbon-hydrogen groups and shows fast signal decay after air exposure. The result links the starting design to how it conducts, vibrates, and reacts to air.
arxiv-2604-21896: Tan, Wang, and Guo introduce Nemobot, an environment for game agents powered by large language models, toward self-programming AI. It extends Claude Shannon's taxonomy of game-playing machines. A chatbot inside shows skill across four game classes. Dictionary games compress state-action mappings into general models. Solvable games use maths reasoning for optimal strategies and readable explanations. Heuristic games blend minimax insights with crowd data. Learning games use reinforcement learning with human feedback and self-critique. Users can create and deploy agents there, experimenting with generation and fine-tuning.
arxiv-2604-21996: An and Nie look at solar-reflected dark matter, up-scattered by fast electrons in the Sun, giving a high-velocity tail that can enhance signals. They study an inelastic model, in which solar scattering fills the excited state, and de-excitation in detectors releases the mass-splitting energy, helping the release exceed the threshold. Monte Carlo simulations give velocity and energy distributions of solar-reflected inelastic dark matter across masses and splittings. Their results show xenon and semiconductor experiments can place constraints on MeV-scale inelastic dark matter.
arxiv-2604-22296: Singla, Patel and Dube evaluate open-source tools for simulating lunar images. Such images help plan landings, spot hazards and test navigation before a mission flies. The study focuses on how camera models and lighting conditions affect image quality. It uses real elevation models and terrain data from Chandrayaan-2 and NASA cameras. The aim is more reliable synthetic imagery for autonomous navigation and decision-making in lunar exploration, plus a better understanding of the Moon's surface.
arxiv-2604-22596: Ghanbari and 12 colleagues report a setup tracking frequency shifts in superconducting radio cavities at DESY. Frequency and quality factor shifts across the superconducting to normal transition reveal the cavity sample's traits. That insight matters for niobium ones modified near the surface with interstitial oxygen and nitrogen, giving novel traits not yet grasped. In its run the system measures the electron mean free path within the penetration depth and the normal skin depth. It also enables study of an odd shift dip near the critical temperature.
arxiv-2604-22696: Salomoni, Datchi, Saitta, and France-Lanord model liquid sulfur with atom-scale force rules learned by machine learning, to chart its lambda change, the heat-driven joining of ring molecules into chains. At normal pressure they catch eight-sulfur rings melting, then show rings of other sizes sparking the change. They map the joining phase chart up to middle pressures.
arxiv-2604-23096: Jung, Koo, and Shin study modular functions with rational Fourier coefficients and ask when a scaled variant stays integral over the ring Z[j]. Here j is the elliptic modular function, and the scaled form divides the argument by a prime p. When p is congruent to 1 or minus 1 modulo N, they show that a product expression built from f and its scaled form stays integral over Z[j]. The result extends the classical Kronecker congruence relation for j to this wider family.
arxiv-2604-23196: Karbab builds AsmRAG, a malware detector that treats detection as evidence-based retrieval over assembly code, not opaque statistical classification. A code-specialised language model turns assembly functions into semantic vectors, forming a searchable base that resists syntactic hiding. A Density-Weighted Anchor Selection step then isolates the core malicious logic in a binary, yielding checkable forensic proof that resists evasion. On 40,000 binaries it reaches 96 percent detection F1 and 95 percent family attribution F1, holding up against metamorphic hiding where EMBER and ResNeXt degrade.
arxiv-2604-23396: Mekonnen and colleagues reproduce a planning trick for generative retrieval, in which a look-ahead signal guides the search for document identifiers before ordinary decoding begins. Their checks confirm the reported gains on standard retrieval tests, but they also find the planning signal fragile: small wording changes such as typos can collapse the planned candidate set. Translating non-English queries back into English recovers the most lost ground, the authors report.
arxiv-2604-23596: Brandt and Mehlmann give a rigorous analysis plus simulations of a landfast ice model for Arctic sea ice attached to the coast or grounded, hence nearly motionless. The model extends the classic viscous-plastic framework with tensile strength and threshold-dependent basal stress. They prove local and global well-posedness results plus time-periodic solutions, and simulations reveal stationary equilibria with vanishing ice velocity, matching the theory.
arxiv-2604-23896: Raees and Papangelis review how right use of AI advice is measured in human-AI decision research, setting it apart from trust and mere reliance. They find the ideas about right use remain scattered across studies. They present three views found in past work, Traditional, Appropriateness, and Dominance, and weigh the hard metrics reported under each. They argue for shared metrics to enable study-to-study comparison and examine metric validity in context.
arxiv-2604-23996: Bo and eight colleagues propose SMoES, a routing scheme that lets vision-language mixture-of-experts models specialize experts by modality. Soft scores track how modalities fuse at each layer, experts are grouped for parallel deployment, and a regularization term keeps specialization coherent across groups. Across four models and 16 benchmarks it improves accuracy, cuts expert-parallel communication by more than half, and raises throughput.
arxiv-2604-24096: Kim and five colleagues improve respiratory sound classification by training base models on varied data splits. Models trained on identical data overfit together and make correlated errors, dulling ensemble gains. Their meta-ensemble trains bases on fixed and cross-validated splits at patient and sample levels, then merges outputs through a trained meta-model. It sets a new best on the ICBHI benchmark with a score of 66.49 percent, and it also transfers better to two outside datasets.
arxiv-2604-24596: Medhi and four colleagues present the first grid-based stellar evolution study of HD 20794, a nearby metal-poor dwarf hosting a compact planetary system with a super-Earth near the habitable zone. Computing 252 models and fitting temperature, gravity, luminosity, radius and age, they favor an age of about 9 billion years. The best models reproduce the observed surface abundances, including phosphorus and chlorine, consistent with enrichment by core-collapse supernovae.
arxiv-2604-24696: Wang and nine colleagues present NeuroClaw, a multi-agent helper for runnable and checked neuroimaging research. Brain data come in many forms, and long chains of steps make drift easy. It works on raw data across structural, functional and diffusion MRI plus EEG, grounding decisions in dataset meaning and BIDS metadata. Pinned setups, Docker support, checkpoints and audit traces make toolchains clear. Three tiers split user contact, planning and tool skills into safe units. The goal is work others can rerun and check.
arxiv-2604-25096: Mehta and eight colleagues model bidirectional false belief amplification in human-chatbot dialogue. From chat logs of individuals showing delusional thinking, they develop a latent state model. The model captures influences between humans and chatbots that accumulate and decay. A bidirectional influence model beats a unidirectional alternative, in which humans primarily drive delusion. Human influence on chatbots is strong but short-lived, while chatbot influence on humans lasts longer. Chatbots also show strong and stable self-influence over future outputs of their own, tending to perpetuate delusions over long stretches.
arxiv-2604-25496: Bendib, Perrin-Gilbert and Sigaud improve zero-shot offline RL via behavioral task sampling. Offline zero-shot RL aims to learn agents optimizing unseen rewards with no further environment interaction. The standard approach trains task-conditioned policies by sampling task vectors. In most existing algorithms, these vectors are randomly sampled, but they argue this leads to suboptimal zero-shot generalization. Instead, task vectors come from the offline dataset to define the training task distribution. Across multiple benchmarks, their approach improves zero-shot performance by an average of 20 percent.
arxiv-2604-25896: Vališka and six colleagues use ultrasound velocity measurements on an ultraclean UTe2 crystal to complete its phase diagram's tetracritical topology. Measurements run up to 18 tesla with field along the b-axis. A sharp non-hysteretic anomaly appears in one longitudinal mode, with a weaker response in a second and none in a third. A kink in transverse magnetostriction accompanies it. Together they show symmetry-selective coupling to lattice strain. The new phase line stays nearly constant near 14 tesla and meets three other boundaries at a tetracritical point.
arxiv-2604-25996: Nalewajko and three co-authors simulate saturated inflow toward a rapidly spinning Kerr black hole. They analyze one eruption-buildup flux cycle. After it, the weakened jet develops a strong helical distortion. The poloidal field along the jet core survives it unchanged. Toroidal lines ejected during the blast, later drawn back, form field detours along the inner sheath. Such distortion may appear as an uneven faster-than-light knot in thick-accretion sources. The re-powered jet section tilts a few degrees, shifting light boost toward BL Lac viewers.
arxiv-2604-26296: Zhao and three colleagues probed how far frozen semantic priors can rescue neural speech coding at ultra-low bitrates. Meaning cues from HuBERT and Whisper cut word errors by about 10 percent at 1.5 kbps, yet the gain faded past 6 kbps, marking a practical capacity edge. HuBERT kept tone and timbre better, while Whisper curbed invented words in noise and closed the gap for unseen speakers. A bitrate-aware rule then tunes prior strength to balance meaning against natural sound.
arxiv-2604-26396: Dong, Han, and Yao proved that large matrices built from consistent rank correlations, such as Hoeffding's D, follow the semicircle law in the proportional high-dimensional regime. Earlier work had shown Kendall's tau and Spearman's rho matrices converge to the Marchenko-Pastur law instead. The result generalizes their own recent work on Chatterjee's rank correlation, the first semicircle result for a large correlation matrix. It draws a sharp line between different families of rank-based matrices.
arxiv-2604-26996: Okite and three colleagues argue that personalization benchmarks confuse semantic closeness with situational fit, leaving it unclear whether systems truly grasp what a user needs in context. They introduce the Proximity Advantage score, a metric for closeness bias, and LUCid, a benchmark of 1,936 user queries paired with long interaction logs. Across retrieval, reranking, and generation stages, performance collapses: retrieval recall falls near zero on the hardest cases, and response alignment stays near 50 percent even for leading models. The gap reveals a basic mismatch between encoded relevance and real user needs.
arxiv-2604-27196: McDonald extends a technical result on scores of tilted distributions, tools used in score-based diffusion models. Earlier work covered a linear tilt of a reference measure. Scores under convolution with a normal variable then follow from convolutions of the original density. He adds constant negative diagonal tilts to that account. A linear tilt shifts the score operator in location. A quadratic tilt shifts it in both location and time. Tilted scores thus read as original scores at a different place and noise level.
arxiv-2604-27296: Cheng and six colleagues tackle efficient code editing with large language models. Full-code generation creates severe efficiency bottlenecks for interactive assistants needing low latency and cost. The edit format itself has been largely overlooked in training. Conventional diff formats suffer fragile offsets and fragmented hunks that make generation unnatural. They introduce BlockDiff and FuncDiff. These structure-aware diff formats represent changes as block-level rewrites of coherent units such as control structures and functions. They also propose AdaEdit, a general adaptive editing approach.
arxiv-2604-27596: Liu and six colleagues introduce SECOS, a method for rigorous classification in open-world semi-supervised learning, where unlabeled data hold known and novel classes. Older methods fail here because novel samples lack explicit supervision and models cannot extract latent semantics, so predicted labels may not match candidate text labels. SECOS predicts textual labels directly from the candidate set, using external knowledge to align semantic representations across modalities. Even against rivals judged under lenient post-hoc matching, SECOS surpasses them by up to 5.4 percent without such help.
arxiv-2604-27696: Girolimetto and three colleagues present FoReco and FoRecoML, R tools for forecast matching of many constrained time series. Full software jointly doing cross-sectional, time, and cross-time matching was lacking, and these tools fill the gap. FoReco covers old and regression-based linear methods, while FoRecoML covers non-linear machine learning methods. Easy defaults let new users apply methods with minimal effort, while experts keep full control to explore extras through custom settings.
arxiv-2604-27796: Kumaravelu, Gupta, and Srijith propose Post-Optimization Adaptive Rank Allocation, a data-free Low-Rank Adaptation trimming method fitting fine-tuning pipelines. Standard LoRA sets the same rank across layers, ignoring inner depth and causing waste. PARA prunes LoRA ranks using a global core-value threshold across layers, yielding non-uniform ranks based on layer-wise signal weight. As a post-hoc method, PARA avoids training changes and wobble, cutting weights by 75 to 90 percent while keeping scores across vision and language benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-27996: Vonderhorst and colleagues compare agent designs for turning plain-language requests into scientific visualisation workflows across fifteen benchmark tasks. General coding agents succeed most often but cost more, domain-specific agents run cheaper and steadier yet flex less, and computer-use agents handle single steps but falter on longer workflows. Persistent memory helps over repeated trials, though its value depends on interaction mode and feedback quality.
arxiv-2605-00196:
Tomasz J. Kozubowski, Andrey Sarantsev, and James A. Spiker develop a statistical law for data that pairs a main variable with the spread behind it. Their bivariate model grows out of the generalized Laplace distribution, built as a normal mixture whose variance is driven by a gamma variable. The twist is that the gamma variable is observed too, not hidden.

With both parts observed, maximum likelihood fitting becomes far simpler than in the usual one-variable case, reducing to a form of classic linear regression. The authors write out the estimators in explicit form. For some parameter settings the estimators converge faster than the usual square-root rate. They close by fitting the model to returns and volatility of several major stock indices.
arxiv-2605-00496:
Yongpeng Cao and Yuji Yamakawa test whether faster video makes unfamiliar human actions easier for AI to understand without any task-specific training. Zero-shot understanding matters where actions are rapid or rare, since labeled examples are scarce. Their case study is kendo, the Japanese fencing art, whose strikes are quick and subtle.

Their training-free pipeline pairs a pretrained video-language model, which supplies semantic representations, with language-model reasoning that compares actions pairwise. The same scenes were tested at three frame rates, from thirty to one hundred twenty frames per second. Higher frame rates clearly improved how well action meanings separated in the zero-shot setting. Adding tracked body-joint information helped under both full and partial views. The authors conclude that high-speed perception yields steadier, more interpretable representations of fast action.
arxiv-2605-00896:
Prabhjot Singh and Manmeet Singh challenge the move toward complex vision models for InSAR phase unwrapping, a key bottleneck in volcanic and seismic monitoring from satellite radar. Their large ablation study on a global benchmark finds a clear complexity penalty. A plain U-Net with fewer parameters beats attention-based models by wide margins on fit and error, and runs much faster.

Spectral analysis explains why. Attention captures sharp edges in natural images, but it injects unphysical high-frequency artifacts into smooth geophysical fields, breaking the smoothness that elastic deformation requires. The plain model is also the only candidate comfortably meeting the speed needed for operational early warning. The authors advocate physics-informed simplicity for such regression tasks.
arxiv-2605-00996:
Andrey Kupavskii and Georgy Sokolov determine the largest family of subsets of an n-element set that contains no s pairwise disjoint sets, in a specific parameter regime. The condition links the family size to parameters written through n as a multiple plus a remainder, with s large enough relative to those parameters. Families avoiding a matching of size s are a central object in extremal combinatorics.

The result can be read as a non-uniform analogue of results tied to the Erdős Matching Conjecture, in the regime where the clique construction is extremal. By settling the other end of the problem from earlier cases, the authors complete the picture for this range and clarify which structure truly maximizes the family.
arxiv-2605-01096:
Devdutt Subhasish and two co-authors show that a small underactuated unicycle robot can learn to race around a track in minutes, learning directly from real-world interaction. Reinforcement learning could push robots with fast, unstable dynamics to their performance limits, but most successes rely on carefully built simulators and domain randomization for transfer to real hardware. The authors bypass simulators entirely.

They use Infoprop Dyna, an uncertainty-aware model-based reinforcement learning framework described as state of the art. With that method, the Mini Wheelbot learns to race within eleven minutes of real-world experience. The result shows that modern model-based learning can handle fast, nonlinear, unstable hardware without a physics simulator. That shortens the path from algorithm to physical performance.
arxiv-2605-01196:
Ali Gürbüz and five co-authors study how surface viscosities affect the motion of a droplet that encloses a translating rigid particle, in slow Stokes flow.
